second_read.reason: The paper explicitly describes the design as 'a Difference-in-Difference with a staggered roll-out of treatment', cites Goodman-Bacon and Sun-Abraham, and reports Callaway-Sant'Anna event studies alongside TWFE (Figures 3, 5, 6). But no main-text specification is clean: the static Equations 1 and 3 (Tables 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) code treatment as a categorical count of entries (One / Two / Three+ DS entries) rather than a binary indicator, and every table and both event-study equations (Eq. 2 with beta*X_it household demographics; Eq. 4 with beta*X_lbt local population, income, rents, their growth rates, and business density) include time-varying controls. Table 7 column 1 (tract FE + year FE) still includes demographic controls. The event-study figures print no coefficients.

County-by-year FE in the tract panel would be allowed on its own. Treatment is absorbing (entry 'has occurred by t'), so no switch-off problem. design: Bandit pricing model plus descriptive product-day data from one e-commerce retailer (113,024 products, Jun-Dec 2019); empirical tests compare long-tail products that are monitored vs. never monitored across a single pre/post split (Jun-Aug vs. Sep-Dec 2019).
reason: The main contribution is a bandit model solved by simulation; the empirical section (Tables 4-6) is a two-period, two-group comparison with one common post date for all products, where 'treatment' is a time-invariant monitoring-group indicator, plus time-varying price controls and matching weights. There is no staggered adoption, and the authors present the results as associations.
appendix_only_specs: Web Appendix B.2 'event study'-type analysis of focal price responses to competitor price changes, and Web Appendix D daily-level robustness of Tables 4-6; neither is a staggered binary TWFE design as described.
notes: Theory-plus-descriptive paper; treatment intensity (low/medium/high monitoring) and three-way interactions in Tables 4-6.
data_statement: Data provided under an NDA and data use agreement; authors state they will be limited to sharing 'only disguised aggregate partial data'.

design: Listing-level repeated cross-section of ~27,900 Boston and Pittsburgh homes (June 2019-May 2022); treatment is the single November 2021 Zillow iBuyer shutdown, compared with the same months in two prior June-May cycles (Treated Year x After November).
reason: There is one common event date (November 2021) and the comparison group is prior-year seasonal cycles, not untreated units in calendar time, so there is no staggered adoption. Table 2 column 1 is FE-only (ZIP and list-week FE; After November x Treated Year 0.011, SE 0.002), but the design is a single-date across-year DiD; Tables 3-5 add time-varying controls.
appendix_only_specs: Appendix C Tables 7, 8, 11 and 12 repeat the same single-event across-year design or are correlational.
notes: One of Davide Proserpio's own papers (Troncoso, Malik, Proserpio, Fu). Also includes an online between-subjects experiment (Appendix A) and a stylized theory model.
data_statement: Data Availability statement: the data are publicly available on the platform subject to access limits, and 'the processed data and replication code used in this study will be made available on request'.
